chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who exchanges the Kufiyya coin for the Shamiyya coin, weight for weight. The money-changer says, 'I will not exchange for you until you exchange for me a Yusufiyya for a Ghillah, weight for weight.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.' We said, 'Indeed, the money-changer only sought the surplus of the Yusufiyya over the Ghillah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.الشَّامِيَّةُ: A type of silver coin from Syria.
key_terms.الْكُوفِيَّةُ: A type of silver coin used in early Islamic times.
key_terms.غِلَّةٌ: A type of silver coin, often implying a specific weight or purity.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay an extra coin when exchanging different types of currency of the same metal?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a specific commercial practice where a money-changer (Sarraaf) demands a surplus coin (Yusufiyya) to offset the inferior quality of another coin (Ghillah) in a weight-for-weight exchange. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between riba al-fadl (excess in exchange of same commodity) and legitimate trade adjustments for quality differentials, emphasizing that the surplus is for value compensation rather than interest on a loan. The hadith underscores the practical flexibility in early Islamic currency markets, where varying metallic purity necessitated such compensatory mechanisms.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who exchanges the Kufiyan (coin) with the Syrian (coin), weight by weight. So the money-changer is saying, ‘I will not change for you until you change for me a Yusufiyya with a price with a profit, weight by weight. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’. So we said, ‘But rather the money-changer sought the extra Yusufiyya upon the profit’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ibn Muskan from Muhammad al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who exchanged al-Kufiy (dirham) for al-Shamiy in equal weight, and the exchanger said, ‘I will not exchange it for you unless you exchange for me invalid Yusufiyah in equal weight . 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful . 5 We then said, ‘The exchanger asked for the extra of invalid al-Yusufiyah only . 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful . 555
